name: Breadcrumb relationship confusion
summary: Presenting visit history or required transaction stages as hierarchical ancestors misrepresents the information relationship.
recurring_structure: Breadcrumb-looking trail is populated with prior visited URLs or wizard steps even when they are not actual parent/ancestor pages.
harm_mechanism: The labels/separators imply false ancestry and can lead users to an unrelated conceptual parent or mistake progress for site structure.
context: Multilevel site or sequential service with a breadcrumb-like link trail.
applicability: Breadcrumb is presented as site ancestry but items encode history or chronological process.
legitimate_contexts: A separately labelled recent-pages history list.
A clearly labelled transaction progress indicator or stepper.
A dynamic hierarchy whose actual parent changes by content context.

usability: Users might infer wrong parent location; not measured with users.
accessibility: Page-location explanation may be misleading; no individual implementation accessibility audit.
maintainability: IA and UI wording can diverge when history is mistaken for taxonomy; no empirical maintenance result.

counterexamples.summary: An explicit progress component truthfully represents ordered steps without claiming site hierarchy.

version_context: GOV.UK, USWDS, Primer first-party docs unpinned; no task research
